page.introBody: Jev (TypeSafe AI's System One model) is a discriminative model that never chats or writes code: you give it a state and typed questions (yes-no noul / multiple-choice / ordered score), and it returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities. It fits cheap judgment tasks like intent classification, routing, moderation and scoring. The official Jev is a closed cloud model available only through its remote API — connect via the official endpoint, OpenRouter, or a compatible relay.

page.agentHint: Once configured, agents can call this capability in sessions through the typed_decide tool for classification, routing, and scoring.
delegate.title: Approval delegation
delegate.subtitle: Let the decision model auto-approve high-confidence approvals.
delegate.enabledHint: Pending approvals are judged by the decision model first; only high-confidence ones skip interrupting you
delegate.allowThresholdHint: Auto-approve when p(approve) reaches this value (0.5–1, default 0.9); below it, the session permission mode applies as usual (you get asked)
delegate.safetyHint: The model can only grant convenience, never deny: anything not approved inherits the current session permission mode. Hard blocks, sensitive operations like password entry, and file edits requiring diff review are never delegated; model errors fall back to manual approval.
delegate.noKeyHint: No API key configured — delegation has no effect yet.
delegate.verifyActionsHint: After act_ui runs, the decision model checks natural-language expectations against the resulting UI state, replacing a full primary-model turn
